newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African gold mines post Q2 losses, worse to come.
newsitem.headline: S.African gold mines post Q2 losses, worse to come.

text.p: South African gold mines plunged into the red for the first time ever in the second quarter, and analysts said on Wednesday things would get worse before they get better.

The South African gold mining industry made an aggregate 180 million rand ($39.2 million) loss in the June quarter after deductions for capital expenditure, said Nick Goodwin, analyst at Fesure Asset Management.

"This is the first time the industry has had negative earnings," he said, adding that the industry made a 257 million rand profit in the March quarter, and the figure was as much as 688 million rand in the June quarter only a year ago.
Goodwin warned that industry losses could total 400 million rand in the September quarter.
The current weak bullion price -- last trading in London close to 12-year lows at $327.80/328.30 an ounce -- is expected to make its mark in the September quarter, hitting marginal mines hard.

"The marginal operations suffered the most this (June) quarter, and they are likely to have another difficult quarter because of the gold price," Dave Giese at Merrill Lynch (Smith Borkhum) told Reuters.
Analysts said more and more mines were becoming marginal, and further job losses were expected in the current quarter.
But news was not all bad, analysts said, noting the industry managed to improve production slightly in the second quarter to 117,824 kg of gold from 117,213 kg in the March quarter.

"Production seems to have stabilised and I'm sure it's not going to fall much further. It could perhaps even increase," Goodwin said, referring to the recent productivity-linked wage agreement aimed at boosting gold output by 90 tonnes this year.
South Africa produced 495 tonnes of gold in 1996.
With the exception of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd whose earnings were more or less steady, South African mining houses saw second quarter income fall substantially.
Marginal mining specialist Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd fell to a pre-capex cash loss of 40.95 million rand from 54.99 million rand the previous quarter.
Anglo saw its June quarter available profit dip two percent to 220.7 million rand -- saved by a well-managed hedging programme, analysts said.

Analysts said Anglo's hedging programme helped it achieve an average gold price of 1,638 rand/ounce in the June quarter, when the average gold price received for the industry in the same period was 1,599 rand/ounce.
"Anglo's results were very good. They've been locking in prices for years. What they made from hedging is almost the equivalent of a whole new mine," Goodwin said.

Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, with its traditional policy of non-hedging, achieved an average price of 1,537 rand/ounce and its second quarter pre-capex profit fell to 192.34 million rand from 236.42 million rand in the March quarter.

In presenting interim results for the March quarter, all six mining houses made clear to analysts and investors how they intended to cut costs and raise production. But analysts doubted any turnaround was likely in the current quarter.
"I don't really think they'll manage to pull right this quarter. But every company, without exception, has told us what steps they're taking to reduce costs and to increase production.
"Whether they can turn it around in a three month period remains to be seen," Giese said.

Analysts said the effects of the recent productivity-linked wage agreement between the Chamber of Mines employer body and the National Union of Mineworkers would not show through until the fourth quarter.
-- Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003 ($ = 4.589 South African Rand)
